decisions.reason: ACE3 was publicly launched as setting a new industry standard and is central to the firm's core airfield lighting control business, so the investment and public commitment strongly favor continuation.

The air situation display supports the tower and surveillance portfolio and was given its own page, so it fits the announced integrated-operations direction and any weak results can be attributed to the temporary pandemic slump in air traffic.
Training programs cost little to maintain and complement the firm's service offering, and pandemic-related dips in demand are plausibly temporary.
The airfield ground lighting course builds on the core lighting business at low cost, although its lower visibility makes it somewhat more expendable or likely to be folded into broader training.
Collaboration software is central to the announced direction of collaborative decision-making and real-time information sharing, so management would persist with it.

The MLAT system was announced as a flagship at inter airport Europe 2019, and that strong public commitment, the sunk R&D, and its fit with the surveillance strategy make dropping it very unlikely despite the COVID-era market weakness.
